for: The experts' risk-mapping sign-off (G6), to ship as content 5.2.0. Nothing here is approved.
notes: gaps is an ordered list: the first area heads the question in the working report (lib/documents/workingReport.ts:44-54).
role in optionGapMap is carried as in 5.1.0 but is not signed: the risk-mapping payload keeps area ids only (lib/content/signoffs.ts:60-70).
controlsShown lists the controls the question page offers before any checklist option is ticked, in the order shown.

Q-PP-01.text: Have you checked whether AI is the best approach, compared with simpler options such as a statistical model, a set of rules or a manual process?
Q-PP-01.reason: "checked whether AI is the best approach … simpler options" is PP-01 (techno-solutionist bias) and C-01 (alternatives analysis) word for word.

Q-PP-02.text: Have you clearly defined the problem your AI system aims to solve, including specific objectives and success criteria?
Q-PP-02.reason: "defined the problem … objectives and success criteria" belongs in problem formulation, where PP-01 says the bias is introduced. No control covers writing a problem statement or success measures; C-02 is the nearest.
Q-PP-02.note: Needs a control the 28 do not have (problem statement and success criteria).

Q-PP-03.text: Have you identified all stakeholders who are directly or indirectly affected by the AI system?
Q-PP-03.reason: "identified all stakeholders" is PP-04's first mitigation (stakeholder mapping) and C-07. The area also shows C-03 and C-05, which are data audits; that is the cost of controls attaching per area.

Q-PP-04.text: Have you assessed how the AI system might affect protected or vulnerable groups, for example by gender, age, ethnicity, disability or income?
Q-PP-04.reason: "affect protected or vulnerable groups" is C-06 (protected group identification) under PP-03 and C-07 under PP-04.

Q-PP-05.text: Have you conducted a human rights impact assessment for the AI system?
Q-PP-05.reason: A human rights impact assessment touches PP-03 (societal harm) and PP-04 (who is served), so the areas stand. Unsure: no impact-assessment control is reached; C-02, whose resources include the EU AI Act Art. 27 assessment, sits only under PP-01 and PO-05.
Q-PP-05.note: Experts: add C-02 to PP-03, map this question to PP-01 as well, or accept that no control fits.

Q-PP-24.text: Have you checked which perspectives the problem needs (disciplines, lived experience, gender, language and culture of the people affected) and brought in the ones your team lacks?
Q-PP-24.reason: "checked which perspectives the problem needs … brought in the ones your team lacks" is C-20 (multi-stakeholder consultation), and PP-01's `mitigated` text names "stakeholder consultation during problem definition". This is CG-19, which the 5.0.0 sitting deferred as a mapping change (SITTING-1.md:424). PP-01 goes last so the report heading stays PP-03.

Q-PP-07.text: Have you estimated the energy use and carbon cost of the proposed AI system?
Q-PP-07.reason: "energy use and carbon cost" is PO-05's definition, and C-02 lists CodeCarbon. Under the PO-05 row it suggests C-02 and C-01 instead of C-02 and C-26.

Q-PP-08.text: Have you documented the data sources, collection methods, and rationale for data selection?
Q-PP-08.reason: "documented the data sources" is PO-07 (documentation deficit), and C-19 (datasheet) is the practice. Under the PO-07 row C-26 drops out; C-17 and C-28 remain as related documentation.

Q-PP-09.text: Have you assessed whether your training data is representative of the target population?
Q-PP-09.reason: Same areas, new order. "representative of the target population" is PP-04's definition (design population does not match the population served), so PP-04 should head the report, not PP-02 (data too sparse).

Q-PP-11.text: Have you checked whether any input could stand in for a sensitive attribute (for example, village standing in for ethnicity), and decided what to do about it?
Q-PP-11.reason: "input could stand in for a sensitive attribute" is a route for historical and societal bias (PP-03); C-04 and C-06 fit.
Q-PP-11.note: IP-01 (algorithmic discrimination) would also fit; the experts may want it second.

Q-PP-12.text: Have you checked that the data labels are correct and consistent?
Q-PP-12.reason: "data labels are correct and consistent" is PP-07 and C-12 (labelling QA).

Q-PP-GATE-SENSITIVE.text: Does your data contain information that could identify a person, or other sensitive personal information?
Q-PP-GATE-SENSITIVE.reason: The gate decides whether Q-PP-13 and Q-PP-14 apply. A gate maps to no risk area (validate.ts, FR-CNT-04), so it stays empty.

Q-PP-13.text: Have you obtained proper informed consent for data collection and use?

Q-PP-14.text: Have you removed or replaced the details in your data that could identify a person (anonymisation or pseudonymisation)?
Q-PP-14.reason: "removed or replaced the details … that could identify a person" is PP-06 and C-10.

Q-PP-16.text: Which of the following data quality assessments have you performed?
Q-PP-16.reason: A checklist: its areas come from the options (see the option table). `gaps` stays empty.

Q-PP-17.text: Which of the following bias types have you assessed for in your data?
Q-PP-17.reason: A checklist: its areas come from the options (see the option table). `gaps` stays empty.

Q-PP-18.text: Have you assessed whether your data collection methods could introduce selection bias?
Q-PP-18.reason: Same areas, new order. "collection methods could introduce selection bias" is PP-05's definition (non-random or uneven sampling), so PP-05 should head the report.

Q-PP-19.text: Have you evaluated whether historical patterns in the data reflect past discrimination or systemic inequities?
Q-PP-19.reason: "historical patterns … reflect past discrimination" is PP-03's definition.

Q-PP-20.text: Have you checked whether your training data is recent enough for the time the system will be used?
Q-PP-20.reason: "recent enough for the time the system will be used" is data relevance (PP-02) and drift (PO-01). PO-01 also brings C-23 (canary rollout), which does not fit a pre-processing check; that is the cost of controls attaching per area.

Q-PP-21.text: Have you established data governance policies covering access, sharing, and retention?
Q-PP-21.reason: "data governance policies covering access, sharing, and retention" is C-09 under PP-06. Under the PO-03 row, drift (C-21) drops out and C-26 (who decides, by role) remains.

Q-PP-22.text: Have you checked whether your data has enough examples of rare cases and conditions?
Q-PP-22.reason: "enough examples of rare cases" is data scarcity (PP-02) and the served population (PP-04).

Q-PP-23.text: Have you engaged domain experts in reviewing data quality and relevance?
Q-PP-23.reason: Swap IP-02 for PP-02. "domain experts … reviewing data quality and relevance" is label checking (PP-07) and relevance (PP-02: data "not relevant to the problem"). Aggregation bias (IP-02) is about pooling groups in a model, not about expert review.

Q-IP-01.text: Have you written down why you chose this type of model for your problem and your data?
Q-IP-01.reason: "why you chose this type of model" touches opacity (IP-03: "selecting interpretable models where appropriate") and IP-04. Unsure: IP-04 is about evaluation metrics, not model choice; C-17 (model card) is the useful control there.
Q-IP-01.note: Experts: keep IP-04, or replace it with PP-01 so C-01 (alternatives) is suggested.

Q-IP-02.text: Have you ensured that training, validation, and test datasets are representative of the same underlying population?
Q-IP-02.reason: Swap IP-01 for PP-05 and lead with it. "training, validation, and test datasets are representative of the same underlying population" is generalisation (PP-05: "causing models to generalize poorly"), with C-05 and C-08 as the practices. Discrimination (IP-01) is not what this question checks.
Q-IP-02.note: Unsure: the split question has no exact area; PP-05 is a pre-processing area, so its controls show "Usually applied in Pre-processing".

Q-IP-03.text: Have you measured the different kinds of error your model makes, for example with a confusion matrix, precision, recall, specificity and F1?
Q-IP-03.reason: "different kinds of error your model makes" is metric choice (IP-04). Under the IP-04 row it suggests C-13, C-14 and C-17 instead of C-13, C-17 and C-18; C-14 is the nearest.
Q-IP-03.note: No control is about measuring error types; see the gaps list.

Q-IP-04.text: Have you calculated performance metrics separately for each relevant subgroup (e.g., by age, gender, ethnicity)?
Q-IP-04.reason: "performance metrics separately for each relevant subgroup" is C-14, reached through IP-01 and IP-02, and C-13.

Q-IP-06.text: Which fairness metrics have you computed?
Q-IP-06.reason: Fairness metrics are IP-01 (C-13). Its `gaps` (IP-01) always shows; the options add IP-02 for the conditional metrics.

Q-IP-07.text: Have you applied explainability methods (e.g., SHAP, LIME, feature importance) to understand model decisions?
Q-IP-07.reason: "explainability methods (e.g., SHAP, LIME …)" is C-18 under IP-03 word for word.

Q-IP-08.text: Have you tested the model on data that differs from its training data, such as noisy, incomplete or unusual inputs?
Q-IP-08.reason: Drop IP-03 and IP-06. "tested the model on data that differs from its training data" is IP-05 (robustness). IP-03 and IP-06 came only from the 5.0.0 merge rule (SITTING-1.md:422), not from the question; reproducibility and opacity are not what it asks.

Q-IP-16.text: Have you compared your model's performance against a simple baseline (e.g., majority class, logistic regression)?
Q-IP-16.reason: Replace IP-04 with PP-01. "compared … against a simple baseline" tests whether the complexity is justified, which is PP-01 and C-01. Under IP-04 it was offered fairness metrics, a model card and explainability (audit sample: WRONG).

Q-IP-17.text: Have you checked whether the model relies on shortcuts in the data that will not hold in real use?
Q-IP-17.reason: "relies on shortcuts in the data" is IP-05 (breaks when data shifts) found with explanations (IP-03, C-18).

Q-IP-18.text: Have you checked whether the model's confidence matches how often it is right?
Q-IP-18.reason: Replace IP-05 with IP-04. "confidence matches how often it is right" is calibration, which Q-IP-13 already maps to IP-04 ("Calibration analysis"); one area for one practice. Neither area has a calibration control.
Q-IP-18.note: No calibration control exists; see the gaps list.

Q-IP-09.text: Have you chosen the simplest model that performs well enough?
Q-IP-09.reason: Add PP-01. "the simplest model that performs well enough" is IP-03 (interpretable models) and the same trade-off as C-01 (alternatives analysis); PP-01 brings C-01.

Q-IP-10.text: Have you recorded everything needed to train the same model again: settings (hyperparameters), random seeds, code and software versions?
Q-IP-10.reason: "recorded everything needed to train the same model again" is IP-06's definition. Under the IP-06 row it suggests C-17, C-19 and C-28 instead of C-17, C-18 and C-19.

Q-IP-11.text: Have you checked that records are not lost or changed as your data is moved and processed?
Q-IP-11.reason: "records are not lost or changed as your data is moved" is IP-07 (data integrity). Under the IP-07 row, anonymisation (C-10) drops out.

Q-IP-12.text: Have you created or updated a model card for this model?
Q-IP-12.reason: Same areas, new order. "created or updated a model card" is documentation (PO-07 lists model cards first), so PO-07 should head the report; C-17 is reached either way.

Q-IP-13.text: Which additional evaluation methods have you applied?
Q-IP-13.reason: A checklist: its areas come from the options (see the option table). `gaps` stays empty.

Q-IP-14.text: Have you considered whether aggregating data across populations masks important subgroup differences?
Q-IP-14.reason: "aggregating data across populations masks … subgroup differences" is IP-02's definition.

Q-IP-15.text: When you tuned the model's settings (for example the decision threshold), did you check that results did not get worse for some groups?
Q-IP-15.reason: "tuned … results did not get worse for some groups" is IP-01 (different outcomes for groups) and IP-04 (the measure optimised).

Q-IP-19.text: Have you assessed whether the model's errors have differential impact across demographic groups?
Q-IP-19.reason: "errors have differential impact across demographic groups" is IP-01 and IP-02.

Q-IP-20.text: Have you documented the model's known limitations, failure modes, and conditions under which it should not be used?
Q-IP-20.reason: Same areas, new order. "documented the model's known limitations" is documentation (PO-07; C-17 covers "where it fails"), so PO-07 should head the report.

Q-IP-21.text: Have you used version control for your code, data processing and trained models?
Q-IP-21.reason: Keep IP-06: "version control for your code, data processing and trained models" is IP-06's first named mitigation ("code versioning"). The fault is IP-06's control list, fixed in the IP-06 row: C-18 (explainability) goes, C-28 comes in.
Q-IP-21.note: Still only a partial fit after the fix: no control is version control; see the gaps list.

Q-IP-22.text: Have you checked whether someone could trick or manipulate the model?
Q-IP-22.reason: "trick or manipulate the model" is robustness (IP-05) and unauthorised modification (IP-07). Neither area has a security or adversarial-testing control.
Q-IP-22.note: No control fits; see the gaps list. The experts may prefer no suggestion here to a partial one.

Q-IP-24.text: Have you tested the model on data from a later time than its training data?
Q-IP-24.reason: "data from a later time than its training data" is IP-05 (distribution shift) and PO-01 (drift).

Q-PO-01.text: Do you regularly check, once the system is in use, whether its performance or its input data have changed?
Q-PO-01.reason: "check … whether its performance or its input data have changed" is PO-01 and C-21.

Q-PO-02.text: Have you defined triggers and procedures for model retraining?
Q-PO-02.reason: "triggers and procedures for model retraining" is C-22 under PO-01.

Q-PO-03.text: Can a person review and overrule the system's outputs before they are acted on?
Q-PO-03.reason: "a person review and overrule the system's outputs" is C-24 under PO-02.

Q-PO-04.text: Have you defined clear roles and responsibilities for AI system outcomes (accountability matrix)?
Q-PO-04.reason: "roles and responsibilities … (accountability matrix)" is C-26 under PO-03.

Q-PO-05.text: Have you created an incident response plan for when the AI system produces harmful outputs?
Q-PO-05.reason: Same areas, new order. "incident response plan" is named in PO-03's `mitigated` text, so PO-03 should head the report; PO-02 adds C-24 (shut the system down).

Q-PO-06.text: Have you provided training or educational resources for end-users of the AI system?
Q-PO-06.reason: "training or educational resources for end-users" is C-27 under PO-04.

Q-PO-07.text: Can end-users understand the AI system's outputs, confidence levels, and limitations?
Q-PO-07.reason: "end-users understand the AI system's outputs, confidence levels, and limitations" is PO-04 (user literacy), with PO-02 for acting on low confidence.

Q-PO-16.text: Have you introduced the system in stages, for example at one site first, before using it everywhere?
Q-PO-16.reason: "introduced the system in stages" is C-23 (canary deployment) under PO-01.

Q-PO-17.text: Once the system is in use, do you check results for each group as well as overall accuracy?
Q-PO-17.reason: Swap PO-06 for IP-01. "check results for each group as well as overall" is subgroup monitoring (C-13, C-14 under IP-01). Feedback loop absence (PO-06) is about people reporting problems, which this question does not ask.

Q-PO-18.text: Have you defined performance thresholds below which the system should be automatically disabled or flagged?
Q-PO-18.reason: "thresholds below which the system should be … disabled or flagged" is PO-01 (monitoring) and PO-02 (C-24: shut down).

Q-PO-08.text: Have you established feedback channels for affected communities and end-users?
Q-PO-08.reason: "feedback channels for affected communities" is PO-06's definition and C-25.

Q-PO-09.text: Is there a mechanism for individuals affected by AI decisions to contest or appeal those decisions?
Q-PO-09.reason: "contest or appeal those decisions" is C-25 under PO-06.

Q-PO-10.text: Have you created complete documentation for the deployed system (codebook, deployment specs)?
Q-PO-10.reason: "documentation for the deployed system (codebook, deployment specs)" is C-28 under PO-07.

Q-PO-11.text: Which of the following governance measures are in place?
Q-PO-11.reason: A checklist: its areas come from the options (see the option table). `gaps` stays empty.

Q-PO-12.text: Have you assessed the AI system's performance across the deployment context's diversity (geographic, linguistic, cultural)?
Q-PO-12.reason: Add IP-02 and lead with it. "performance across the deployment context's diversity (geographic, linguistic, cultural)" is results broken down by group (IP-02: works on average but fails for specific populations; C-14, C-16). PO-01 stays for checking in use.

Q-PO-13.text: Have you planned when and how the AI system will be retired or replaced?
Q-PO-13.reason: Add PO-03 and lead with it. "planned when and how the AI system will be retired" is mainly a decision about who decides and how users and data are handled (PO-03, C-26). PO-05 stays second because the question's good practice counts "the computing and energy the system uses while running".
Q-PO-13.note: No control is about retiring a system. C-09 (data "eventually retired") is the nearest, and this proposal does not reach it. Under it the report lists C-25 (redress) first, which does not fit a retirement plan; the experts may prefer PO-05 first, or adding IP-07 or PP-06 for C-09.

Q-PO-14.text: Does the system handle unusual inputs safely, for example by flagging them for a person instead of giving a confident answer?
Q-PO-14.reason: Drop PO-03. "handle unusual inputs safely … flagging them for a person" is PO-02 (C-24) and PO-01 (detecting inputs unlike training data). PO-03 came from the 5.0.0 merge rule (SITTING-1.md:422), not from the question.

Q-PO-15.text: Have you communicated the AI system's limitations and intended use to all stakeholders?
Q-PO-15.reason: "communicated the AI system's limitations and intended use to all stakeholders" is PO-04 (understanding limitations) and PO-07 (documentation).

Q-PO-20.text: Have you involved representatives of affected communities in the design and evaluation of the AI system?

Q-PO-21.text: Have you assessed the AI system's impact on existing workflows and professional practices?
Q-PO-21.reason: "impact on existing workflows and professional practices" is PO-02 (how people review outputs in their work) and PO-04 (what users understand).

Q-PO-22.text: Have you ensured compliance with applicable data protection regulations and ethical guidelines?

"compliance with applicable data protection regulations" is PP-06, whose `mitigated` text ends "compliance with national data protection laws" (C-09, C-10, C-11). Q-PO-23.text: Have you established regular review cycles to reassess the AI system's appropriateness and performance?
Q-PO-23.reason: "regular review cycles to reassess … appropriateness and performance" is PO-01 (performance) and PO-03 (who decides).

Q-PO-24.text: Have you considered the AI system's impact on equity of access to services?
Q-PO-24.reason: Add PP-04. "impact on equity of access to services" is about who the system serves (PP-04: C-07 maps who is helped or harmed), as well as user literacy (PO-04).
Q-PO-24.note: Unsure: equity of access has no exact area; the experts may prefer IP-01.

PP-01.reason: C-01, C-02 and C-20 are the three practices PP-01's own `mitigated` text names: alternatives analysis, cost-benefit evaluation, stakeholder consultation.

PP-02.name: Data Scarcity & Availability Bias
PP-02.reason: C-03 (completeness) and C-05 (who is missing) match PP-02's "completeness audits, representativeness analysis". C-04 (biases in how data was collected) is a weaker fit for data that is too sparse; kept because nothing closer exists.

PP-03.name: Historical & Societal Bias
PP-03.reason: C-04 (biases baked into the data) and C-06 (protected groups) are PP-03's "contextual bias analysis, protected group identification"; C-03 covers the representativeness side.

PP-04.name: Population Bias

PP-05.name: Sampling & Generalization Bias
PP-05.reason: C-08 (sampling strategy), C-05 and C-03 are PP-05's "stratified sampling … balanced data collection".

PP-06.name: Privacy & Consent Violations
PP-06.reason: C-09, C-10 and C-11 are PP-06's "informed consent protocols, data anonymization techniques, access controls".

PP-07.name: Labeling Bias
PP-07.reason: C-12 (labelling QA) is PP-07's "inter-rater reliability … labeling guidelines"; C-04 covers "who labeled it" and C-03 label accuracy.

IP-01.name: Algorithmic Discrimination
IP-01.reason: C-13, C-14 and C-15 are IP-01's "fairness metrics evaluation, subgroup analysis, and bias mitigation techniques", in that order.

IP-02.name: Aggregation Bias
IP-02.reason: C-14 (disaggregated) and C-16 (stratified or separate models) are IP-02's "disaggregated analysis … separate models"; C-13 measures the subgroup gap.

IP-03.name: Opacity & Unexplainability
IP-03.reason: Drop C-19. A datasheet documents the data, and IP-03 is about decisions nobody can explain; its `mitigated` text names explainability methods and model documentation (C-18, C-17). C-19 stays reached through IP-06 and PO-07.

IP-04.name: Metric Selection Bias
IP-04.reason: Swap C-18 for C-14. IP-04's `mitigated` text is "contextual metric selection, multi-metric evaluation"; C-14 (break performance down by subgroup) is multi-metric evaluation, while C-18 (why the model decides) is not about which metric is used.
IP-04.note: No control is about choosing or reporting error measures (confusion matrix, precision, recall); see the gaps list.

IP-05.name: Model Robustness Failure
IP-05.reason: Replace C-13, C-15 and C-18, none of which tests robustness: fairness metrics, debiasing and explanations. C-14 (performance by subgroup, here by condition or site) and C-21 (catching data drift) are the nearest of the 28 to IP-05's "robustness testing … sensitivity analysis". C-13, C-15 and C-18 stay reached through IP-01 and IP-03.
IP-05.note: None of the 28 controls is a robustness, stress or security test. This row trades three wrong controls for two partial ones; the experts may prefer a new control (see the gaps list).

IP-06.name: Reproducibility Failure
IP-06.reason: Swap C-18 for C-28. IP-06's `mitigated` text is "code versioning, experiment tracking, documentation standards, and model cards"; C-28 documents dependencies and configuration, and explainability (C-18) has nothing to do with reproducing a result.
IP-06.note: No control covers version control or experiment tracking, which IP-06's own text names first; see the gaps list.

IP-07.name: Data Integrity Compromise
IP-07.reason: Drop C-10. IP-07 is "data corruption, unauthorized modification"; anonymisation (C-10) does not prevent either. C-03 (accuracy checks) and C-09 (who may access and change data) match "integrity checks, access controls". C-10 stays reached through PP-06.
IP-07.note: No control is a data-validation pipeline or audit log, which IP-07's text names.

PO-01.name: Deployment Drift
PO-01.reason: C-21 (drift detection), C-22 (retraining) and C-23 (staged rollout) are PO-01's "continuous monitoring … scheduled retraining … drift detection".

PO-02.name: Lack of Human Oversight
PO-02.reason: C-24 (a human can review, override or shut down) is PO-02's core; C-21 supports "validation" and C-25 the override route for people affected.

PO-03.name: Accountability Gap
PO-03.reason: Drop C-21. PO-03 is "no clear ownership … when the AI system produces harmful or incorrect outputs"; drift monitoring is not ownership. C-26 (accountability matrix) and C-25 (redress) match "accountability matrices, incident response". C-21 stays reached through PO-01, PO-02 and IP-05.
PO-03.note: Its text names incident response plans and governance frameworks; no control is an incident-response plan.

PO-04.name: User Literacy Deficit
PO-04.reason: C-27 (user training) is PO-04's "user training programs"; C-24 and C-25 cover knowing when to override and how to complain. C-25 is the weakest of the three.

PO-05.name: Environmental Impact
PO-05.reason: Swap C-26 for C-01. PO-05 is energy and carbon cost; C-26 (who is responsible) does not address it. C-02 lists CodeCarbon among its resources, and C-01 (would a simpler approach do) is PO-05's "efficient model architectures". C-26 stays reached through PO-03.

PO-06.name: Feedback Loop Absence
PO-06.reason: Swap C-27 for C-20. PO-06's `mitigated` text is "feedback platforms, appeal mechanisms, community engagement, and regular stakeholder consultations"; C-20 is multi-stakeholder consultation, while user training (C-27) belongs to PO-04, which still reaches it. This changes Q-PO-09, which the audit sample judged FITS with C-24, C-25 and C-27; it would get C-24, C-25 and C-20.

PO-07.reason: Drop C-26. PO-07's own description lists "model cards, datasheets, codebooks, and deployment specifications": exactly C-17, C-19 and C-28. An accountability matrix is not system documentation. C-26 stays reached through PO-03.
